investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector." No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never produced any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints at all. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable, no VM is provisioned, and the eval runner times out without writing any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is currently confirmed only at the eval layer.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment between 05:46 and 05:51 UTC on 2026-07-02 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm (production-api) has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that every pod the eval attempted to schedule was rejected. The eval runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905 calls createAgent with type "remote", which requires a kata peer-pod VM slot; with none available, the agent pod remained Unschedulable for ~137–147 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect, and is scoped to the eval environment's production-api cluster. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence, so a broader production outage cannot be confirmed from this data alone.

Secondary: The 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector (likely a label or taint requiring kata peer-pod support), meaning the schedulable node pool for remote agents is structurally limited to 2 nodes and cannot expand via preemption ('No preemption victims found').

Tertiary: A concurrent workload spike or leaked/stuck remote-agent pods from a prior eval run may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, preventing new allocations. This is plausible but unconfirmed without node-level resource inspection.

Lower confidence: A node affinity/selector misconfiguration could have reduced the eligible node pool below its intended size, but the message is consistent with the expected 2-node kata pool being simply full rather than misconfigured.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector." No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never produced any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints at all. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable, no VM is provisioned, and the eval runner times out without writing any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is currently confirmed only at the eval layer.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Kubernetes Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in sequence between 05:46 and 05:51 UTC on 2026-07-02 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, no agent was created, no runtime response was produced, and all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent from the eval result.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that match the required node affinity/selector. When the eval runner called createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), the scheduler could not place the resulting pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 affinity-matching nodes had no remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, and the other 4 nodes were excluded by node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable. The pod remained unscheduled for 137–147 seconds across all three checks until each eval timed out, producing empty evidence and a contract validation failure. This is an eval-infrastructure and cluster-capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: existing remote-agent pods or peer-pod VMs are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message across all three sibling checks (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or if nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or relabeled, the effective schedulable pool shrinks further.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) did not complete successfully in a previous run, orphaned pods may be occupying the limited VM resource slots.
Lower confidence — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small to absorb concurrent eval runs plus any background workload.
